Package frc.robot.subsystems.vision

Class Vision

java.lang.Object
edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
frc.robot.subsystems.vision.Vision
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.wpi.first.util.sendable.Sendable, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem
public class Vision extends edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
Fuses AprilTag pose estimates from one or more cameras into a SwerveDrivePoseEstimator (Kalman filter) to produce a single best-estimate robot pose for the aiming and autonomous pipelines.

How the Kalman Filter Works (brief)

The filter maintains a probability distribution over the robot's pose. It has two sources of information:
  • Odometry (wheel encoders + gyro): accurate over short distances but drifts over time. Tuned with m_stateStndDev â€” smaller numbers = trust odometry more.
  • Vision (AprilTag detections): accurate globally but noisy measurement-to- measurement. Tuned with the dynamic stdDevs in periodic() â€” smaller numbers = trust vision more.
The filter blends both sources optimally, weighting each by its stated uncertainty.

Multi-Camera Fusion

Any number of VisionIO instances can be passed to the full constructor. Only those that return true from VisionIO.forPoseEstimation() are used for Kalman filter updates; others may be used for non-localization tasks (e.g., range finding).

Replay Mode

Constructing with the no-arg constructor sets isReplay = true, which bypasses all estimation logic. This is a placeholder for AdvantageKit log-replay â€” the pose would instead come from replayed log inputs rather than live cameras.

  • Method Details

    • periodic

      public void periodic()
      Runs every 20 ms. Performs three stages:
      1. Odometry propagation: updates the Kalman filter with the latest wheel encoder positions and gyro heading. This step runs even when no vision targets are visible and keeps the pose estimate moving correctly between vision updates.
      2. Vision fusion: for each camera flagged for pose estimation, calls VisionIO.getVisionEst() once per loop.
        • Measurements more than 4 m from the current odometry estimate are rejected outright â€” this guards against tag-ID misdetections or extreme lens distortion that would otherwise jump the pose wildly.
        • Accepted measurements are weighted by a distance-scaled standard deviation: Ïƒ = 0.1 + dist * 0.05 for x and y (meters), and Ïƒ = 10Â° + dist * 5Â° for heading. Farther detections are trusted less because pixel errors project to larger field errors at range.
      3. Field2d telemetry: in simulation the field widget shows the ground-truth pose from the drivetrain; on hardware it shows the filter's own estimate.

    • simulationPeriodic

      public void simulationPeriodic()
      Runs every 20 ms in simulation only. Advances the PhotonVision simulation by one step, using the drivetrain's ground-truth pose from m_poseSupplier.

      For cameras mounted on the turret, the camera transform is updated by the current turret rotation before the simulation frame is computed. The rotation is currently hardcoded to 5Â° as a placeholder â€” TODO: replace with the actual turret angle from the Turret subsystem once the turret is wired in (Stage 8).

    • setUpSim

      public void setUpSim()
      Registers the field AprilTag layout and all cameras with the PhotonVision simulation system. Called once from the full constructor when at least one PhotonVisionSimIO is detected in the IO list.
